subproblem.title: Lower integrals over a Lipschitz injective image split along an a.e.-disjoint Borel decomposition
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, E := ℝ^P and H^n := μHE[n]. Let M ⊆ E and A_i ⊆ E (i ∈ ℕ) be sets such that every A_i is Borel, A_i ⊆ M for every i, A_i ∩ A_j = ∅ for i ≠ j, and H^n(M ∖ ⋃_i A_i) = 0. Let φ : E → E be Λ-Lipschitz (Λ ≥ 0) and injective. Then for every g : E → [0, ∞] (no measurability required), ∫⁻_{φ(M)} g dH^n = Σ_{i∈ℕ} ∫⁻_{φ(A_i)} g dH^n.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (M : Set (Euclid P)) (A : ℕ → Set (Euclid P)) (φ : Euclid P → Euclid P) (Λ : NNReal), (∀ i, MeasurableSet (A i)) → (∀ i, A i ⊆ M) → Pairwise (fun i j => Disjoint (A i) (A j)) → μHE[n] (M \ ⋃ i, A i) = 0 → LipschitzWith Λ φ → Injective φ → ∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞, ∫⁻ y in φ '' M, g y ∂μHE[n] = ∑' i, ∫⁻ y in φ '' A i, g y ∂μHE[n]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (dpf_area_formula_bilipschitz_rectifiable), isolated and with details filled in. Notation: E := ℝ^P (Euclid P), H^n := μHE[n]. Hypotheses: every A_i is Borel; A_i ⊆ M; A_i ∩ A_j = ∅ for i ≠ j; H^n(M ∖ ⋃_i A_i) = 0; φ is Λ-Lipschitz and injective; g : E → [0, ∞] is arbitrary.
1. Each φ(A_i) is Borel. φ is Lipschitz, hence continuous, hence continuous on A_i, and φ is injective on A_i. E is a Polish space and A_i is Borel, so the Lusin–Souslin theorem (Mathlib MeasurableSet.image_of_continuousOn_injOn) shows that φ(A_i) is Borel.
2. The sets φ(A_i) are pairwise disjoint. Let i ≠ j. If y ∈ φ(A_i) ∩ φ(A_j), then y = φ(a) = φ(a') with a ∈ A_i and a' ∈ A_j. Injectivity gives a = a' ∈ A_i ∩ A_j = ∅, a contradiction. (In Lean: (Set.disjoint_image_iff hφinj).mpr applied to the disjointness of A_i and A_j.)
3. ⋃_i φ(A_i) ⊆ φ(M), since A_i ⊆ M gives φ(A_i) ⊆ φ(M) for each i (Set.image_mono). Hence (⋃_i φ(A_i)) ∖ φ(M) = ∅, which has H^n-measure 0.
4. φ(M) ∖ ⋃_i φ(A_i) is H^n-null. Let y ∈ φ(M) ∖ ⋃_i φ(A_i) and write y = φ(x) with x ∈ M. If x ∈ A_i for some i, then y = φ(x) ∈ φ(A_i), contradicting y ∉ ⋃_i φ(A_i). So x ∈ M ∖ ⋃_i A_i, and therefore φ(M) ∖ ⋃_i φ(A_i) ⊆ φ(M ∖ ⋃_i A_i). φ is Λ-Lipschitz on M ∖ ⋃_i A_i, so the Lipschitz image bound for the Euclidean Hausdorff measure (SimonGMT Chapter02 euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image_le_of_lipschitzOn n) gives H^n(φ(M ∖ ⋃_i A_i)) ≤ Λ^n · H^n(M ∖ ⋃_i A_i) = Λ^n · 0 = 0. By monotonicity of measure, H^n(φ(M) ∖ ⋃_i φ(A_i)) = 0.
5. Replacing φ(M) by the union. By 3 and 4, both set differences between φ(M) and ⋃_i φ(A_i) are H^n-null. So φ(M) = ⋃_i φ(A_i) H^n-almost everywhere (Mathlib ae_eq_set). Restricting a measure to two a.e.-equal sets gives the same measure (Measure.restrict_congr_set). Hence ∫⁻_{φ(M)} g dH^n = ∫⁻_{⋃_i φ(A_i)} g dH^n for the arbitrary function g (Mathlib setLIntegral_congr; no measurability of g is used).
6. Countable additivity. By 1 and 2 the sets φ(A_i), i ∈ ℕ, are measurable and pairwise disjoint. The lower Lebesgue integral is countably additive over measurable disjoint pieces for an arbitrary function g : E → [0, ∞] (Mathlib lintegral_iUnion). So ∫⁻_{⋃_i φ(A_i)} g dH^n = Σ_i ∫⁻_{φ(A_i)} g dH^n.
7. Combining 5 and 6 gives ∫⁻_{φ(M)} g dH^n = Σ_i ∫⁻_{φ(A_i)} g dH^n. The argument works for every n ≥ 0 and needs no imports beyond GMT.Ch07.Submission.
proof_key_steps: Each φ(A_i) is Borel by Lusin–Souslin, since φ is continuous and injective.
The sets φ(A_i) are pairwise disjoint because φ is injective.
φ(M) = ⋃_i φ(A_i) up to an H^n-null set: ⋃_i φ(A_i) ⊆ φ(M), and φ(M) ∖ ⋃_i φ(A_i) ⊆ φ(M ∖ ⋃_i A_i), which has measure at most Λ^n · 0.
setLIntegral_congr replaces φ(M) by ⋃_i φ(A_i) for an arbitrary g.
lintegral_iUnion over the measurable disjoint φ(A_i) gives the sum.

subproblem.title: Weighted area identity for φ on one injective Lipschitz piece with the Gram tangential Jacobian
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, E := ℝ^P, H^n := μHE[n], and λ := Lebesgue measure on ℝ^n. Let Q : E → {linear subspaces of E} be an arbitrary map. Let φ : E → E be differentiable and Λ-Lipschitz, and F : ℝ^n → E be L-Lipschitz. Let B ⊆ ℝ^n be Borel, with F injective on B and φ injective on F(B). Assume Q(F(b)) = range DF(b) for λ-a.e. b ∈ B. For x ∈ E let e = (e_a) be the standard orthonormal basis of Q(x) (stdOrthonormalBasis), and let J(x) := (det(Dφ(x)e_a · Dφ(x)e_b)_{a,b})^{1/2}. Then for every g : E → [0, ∞] (no measurability required), ∫⁻_{φ(F(B))} g dH^n = ∫⁻_{F(B)} J(x) g(φ(x)) dH^n(x).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Q : Euclid P → Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (φ : Euclid P → Euclid P) (Λ : NNReal) (F : Euclid n → Euclid P) (L : NNReal) (B : Set (Euclid n)), Differentiable ℝ φ → LipschitzWith Λ φ → LipschitzWith L F → MeasurableSet B → InjOn F B → InjOn φ (F '' B) → (∀ᵐ b ∂(volume.restrict B), Q (F b) = LinearMap.range (fderiv ℝ F b : Euclid n →ₗ[ℝ] Euclid P)) → ∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ≥0∞, ∫⁻ y in φ '' (F '' B), g y ∂μHE[n] = ∫⁻ x in F '' B, ENNReal.ofReal (Real.sqrt (Matrix.det (Matrix.of fun i j : Fin (Module.finrank ℝ (Q x)) => inner ℝ (fderiv ℝ φ x (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ (Q x) i)) (fderiv ℝ φ x (stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ (Q x) j))))) * g (φ x) ∂μHE[n]
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3 and 5 of the parent proof (dpf_area_formula_bilipschitz_rectifiable; Simon Ch. 3, 2.3–2.6, J^M_f = sqrt(det(D_{τ_p}f · D_{τ_q}f)) for an orthonormal basis τ of T_xM), for a single piece, with the tangent field abstracted to Q and details filled in.
Notation:
- E := ℝ^P, H^n := μHE[n], λ := volume (Lebesgue measure) on ℝ^n = Euclid n.
- For a linear map T between finite-dimensional real inner product spaces, normDet(T) ≥ 0 is Mathlib's LinearMap.normDet (the square root of det(T*T)).
- For f : ℝ^n → E, areaJacobianAt f a = normDet(Df(a)) (SimonGMT areaJacobianAt_eq_normDet), where Df(a) := fderiv ℝ f a, which is 0 where f is not differentiable.
- For a linear T : E → E and a subspace V, T|_V := (T : E →ₗ E).domRestrict V.
- J(x) := sqrt(det(⟨Dφ(x)e^x_a, Dφ(x)e^x_b⟩)_{a,b}) with e^x := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ (Q x).
1. Area formula used. SimonGMT Chapter02 weighted_area_formula_lipschitz_injOn states: if f : ℝ^n → E is K-Lipschitz, s ⊆ ℝ^n is Borel, f is injective on s, and w : E → [0, ∞] is arbitrary, then ∫⁻_{f(s)} w dμHE[finrank ℝ ℝ^n] = ∫⁻_s ofReal(areaJacobianAt f a) · w(f(a)) dλ(a). Since finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n (finrank_euclideanSpace_fin), the measure on the left is H^n.
2. Gram identity. Let T : E → E be continuous linear, V a subspace of E, and e := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ V (indexed by Fin (finrank ℝ V)). Then normDet(T|_V) = sqrt(det(⟨T e_a, T e_b⟩)_{a,b}).
 Proof: Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_sq_eq_det_gram, applied to f := T|_V and the orthonormal basis e of V, gives normDet(f)^2 = det(Matrix.gram ℝ (a ↦ f(e_a))). Here f(e_a) = T(e_a), and Matrix.gram ℝ v = Matrix.of (a, b ↦ ⟨v_a, v_b⟩), with the coercion ℝ → ℝ being the identity. So normDet(f)^2 = det(⟨T e_a, T e_b⟩)_{a,b}. Since normDet(f) ≥ 0 (LinearMap.normDet_nonneg), normDet(f) = sqrt(normDet(f)^2) = sqrt(det(⟨T e_a, T e_b⟩)_{a,b}).
 Consequence: if V' and W are subspaces with V' = W, then sqrt(det(⟨T e'_a, T e'_b⟩)_{a,b}) with e' := stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ V' equals normDet(T|_W). Substitute V' = W and apply the identity. In Lean, state this for an arbitrary V' and close it with `rintro V' rfl`; rewriting the equation directly under normDet fails because of the dependent FiniteDimensional instance.
3. The composite. Φ := φ ∘ F is (ΛL)-Lipschitz (LipschitzWith.comp). Φ is injective on B, because F is injective on B, F maps B into F(B), and φ is injective on F(B) (Set.InjOn.comp with mapsTo_image). Also φ(F(B)) = Φ(B) (Set.image_comp).
4. Left side. Apply 1 to f := Φ, s := B, w := g: ∫⁻_{φ(F(B))} g dH^n = ∫⁻_{Φ(B)} g dH^n = ∫⁻_B ofReal(areaJacobianAt Φ b) · g(Φ(b)) dλ(b).
5. Right side. Apply 1 to f := F, s := B and the weight w(x) := ofReal(J(x)) · g(φ(x)), which is arbitrary (no measurability is needed): ∫⁻_{F(B)} ofReal(J(x)) · g(φ(x)) dH^n(x) = ∫⁻_B ofReal(areaJacobianAt F b) · (ofReal(J(F(b))) · g(φ(F(b)))) dλ(b).
6. The integrands of 4 and 5 agree for λ⌞B-a.e. b.
 By Rademacher's theorem (Mathlib LipschitzWith.ae_differentiableAt with the Haar measure λ), the Lipschitz map F is differentiable at λ-a.e. point, hence λ⌞B-a.e. (ae_restrict_of_ae). By hypothesis, Q(F(b)) = range DF(b) for λ⌞B-a.e. b. Fix b with both properties.
 Since φ is differentiable at F(b), the chain rule (fderiv_comp) gives DΦ(b) = Dφ(F(b)) ∘ DF(b). Viewing these as linear maps (ContinuousLinearMap.toLinearMap_comp), Mathlib LinearMap.normDet_comp gives normDet(DΦ(b)) = normDet(Dφ(F(b))|_{range DF(b)}) · normDet(DF(b)).
 By the consequence in 2, with T := Dφ(F(b)), V' := Q(F(b)) and W := range DF(b), we get J(F(b)) = normDet(Dφ(F(b))|_{range DF(b)}). Hence areaJacobianAt Φ b = J(F(b)) · areaJacobianAt F b.
 Since J(F(b)) is a square root and hence ≥ 0, ENNReal.ofReal_mul gives ofReal(areaJacobianAt Φ b) = ofReal(J(F(b))) · ofReal(areaJacobianAt F b). Using Φ(b) = φ(F(b)) and commutativity and associativity of multiplication in [0, ∞], ofReal(areaJacobianAt Φ b) · g(Φ(b)) = ofReal(areaJacobianAt F b) · (ofReal(J(F(b))) · g(φ(F(b)))).
7. Conclusion. By 6 and lintegral_congr_ae for the measure λ⌞B, the right sides of 4 and 5 are equal. Hence ∫⁻_{φ(F(B))} g dH^n = ∫⁻_{F(B)} ofReal(J(x)) · g(φ(x)) dH^n(x), which is the claim. The argument works for every n ≥ 0. Imports: the Lean proof needs Mathlib.Analysis.InnerProductSpace.NormDet and Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter02.AreaLipschitz, which the submission may import; the statement itself needs neither.
proof_key_steps: The weighted injective Lipschitz area formula, with finrank ℝ ℝ^n = n, converts H^n-integrals over f(B) into λ-integrals over B with weight ofReal(normDet Df) and an arbitrary w.
Gram identity: normDet(T|_V) = sqrt det(⟨T e_a, T e_b⟩) for e = stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ V, via normDet_sq_eq_det_gram and normDet ≥ 0.
Φ = φ∘F is Lipschitz and injective on B, and φ(F(B)) = Φ(B). Apply the area formula to Φ with weight g, and to F with weight ofReal(J)·(g∘φ).
For λ⌞B-a.e. b (Rademacher plus the hypothesis on Q): the chain rule and normDet_comp, with range DF(b) = Q(F(b)) and the Gram identity, give normDet(DΦ(b)) = J(F(b))·normDet(DF(b)).
ENNReal.ofReal_mul and lintegral_congr_ae equate the two λ-integrals.
